title: Clutches
subtitle: A clutch connects and disconnects power between two shafts. This week covers the definition, components, advantages/disadvantages, and the most important topic — calculating maximum pressure, minimum pressure and average pressure in a plate clutch under two theories: uniform wear and uniform pressure.
learningOutcome: A clutch connects and disconnects power between two shafts. content.text:
Exam-ready definition (from notes):
A clutch is a mechanical device that connects and disconnects the rotating shaft enabling the interaction of power transmission between 2 rotating components and engages 2 gear-changing. They help distribute load evenly.

items: 1. Clutch disk · 2. Pressure plate · 3. Flywheel · 4. Release bearing · 5. Spring · 6. (additional components per system)
Advantages: Smooth engagement · Solid connection · User friendly & easy to engage · Transmits partial power

content.text: Plate clutch pressure analysis — Uniform Wear Theory
r₁ = outer radius (mm) · r₂ = inner radius (mm) · kl = total axial force (N) = F
n = number of pairs of friction surfaces · μ = coefficient of friction · W = total axial force · R = mean radius

Common mistake — Using R = (r₁+r₂)/2 for uniform PRESSURE — that's wrong. R = (r₁+r₂)/2 is for uniform WEAR only. For uniform pressure, R = 2/3 × [(r₁³−r₂³)/(r₁²−r₂²)]. Mixing these up costs big marks.

items: • Find P_max, P_min, P_ave for a plate clutch given F, r₁, r₂.
• Calculate frictional torque using T = nμWR. Distinguish uniform wear from uniform pressure theory.
